chunk_findings.detail:
`at = text.rfind("
" + head + "
")` still treats a fenced `# ddflow brief` line as the anchor because it only searches for the literal string and cannot know whether that line is inside a code fence. When there is no RESUME slice and the real H1 is at the very beginning, a later fenced line becomes the last match: for example, `_under_resume("# ddflow brief
## Work
```text
# ddflow brief
```
", "", "", "## Open workflow choices
- pick A")` inserts the choices block after the opening fence instead of returning `lead + text`. The Open-workflow-choices heading is then inside the code block and is not rendered as a heading, contradicting the helper’s own “fenced `# ddflow brief` must not steal the anchor” contract.

The new fence detector only toggles on `line.lstrip().startswith("```")`, so Markdown code fences delimited by `~~~` are ignored. Those are valid fenced code blocks, so a tilde-fenced `# ddflow brief` below the view H1 still steals the anchor. For example, `_under_resume("## Resume

`_FENCE_OPEN` and `_fence_closes` both allow any leading whitespace via `^\s*`/`\s*`, but CommonMark code fences may be indented only up to three spaces; a line with four leading spaces is an indented code block, not a fence. Given `_last_heading_line("# ddflow brief

chunk_findings.detail:
`_FENCE_OPEN` and `_fence_closes` treat any `\s*` indent as a fence delimiter, but Markdown only recognizes a fence when it is indented by at most three spaces. # ddflow brief
## Work
```text
    ```
# ddflow brief
```
"` and lead `"## Open workflow choices
- pick A"`, `_under_resume` splices the choices between `    ```
` and the inner `# ddflow brief` instead of before the view H1, which is the same in-fence insertion this change is supposed to stop.

chunk_findings.detail:
`_FENCE_OPEN` now rejects valid tilde fences whose info string contains a tilde via `~{3,}(?![^~]*~)`, but CommonMark tilde fences allow any info string after the opening run (`~{3,}.*`). For example, `_last_heading_line("## Resume
# ddflow brief
## Work
~~~text has~tilde
# ddflow brief
~~~
", "# ddflow brief")` fails to enter the `~~~text has~tilde` fence, so it treats the fenced `# ddflow brief` as the last heading, and `_under_resume` splices workflow choices/reports into the code fence instead of under the RESUME slice. The backtick branch is fine, but the same no-fence-char rule does not apply to tilde fences.

chunk_findings.detail: The new filter only removes paths that are not in `GIT.files(cwd, "tracked")`; it does not apply the review's `exclude_globs`, so a tracked file the gate did not cover is still named. For example, if `snapshots/golden.json` is tracked and excluded from review via `[review].exclude_globs`, and it is the only file that differs between the base tree and the gate tree, `tracked` contains `snapshots/golden.json`, so `paths` still contains it and `_what_differs` names it. This leaves the reported “golden snapshots and transcripts” part of B-stale-mark-names-merge-temp-and-excluded-files unfixed; the added regression test only asserts that `.merge_file_4zU3jH` is absent, not that an excluded tracked file is absent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/stale_why.py:_what_differs

chunk_findings.detail: The bug this change claims to close is two cases: merge temps tracked nowhere, and tracked files the review never covers (golden snapshots and transcripts matched by `[review].exclude_globs`). The new filter only drops paths absent from `GIT.files(cwd, "tracked")`. A tracked `snapshots/foo.golden` or `transcripts/run.json` that `exclude_globs` keeps out of the review is still in that set, so `_what_differs` still names it. Given a clean `HEAD`, a worktree whose only difference is that excluded golden file, and `own=None` (the call the new test uses), the note still contains the golden path, so the STALE mark still cannot be cleared by reviewing the covered code. The regression test never builds an excluded-but-tracked path, so it stays green while that half of B-stale-mark-names-merge-temp-and-excluded-files is unchanged.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/stale_why.py:32

chunk_findings.detail: `GIT.files(cwd, "tracked")` is the index-tracked set. A staged deletion (`git rm tracked.py`) removes `tracked.py` from the index, but `differing_paths` still returns it for the same base because the recorded worktree no longer has it. Since `tracked.py` is not in `GIT.files(cwd, "tracked")`, `_gate_covered` drops it, so the stale note does not name a deletion/rename even though the deleted file was tracked in the base and was a change the gate covered. Example: `git rm tracked.py`, then call `_what_differs(cwd, "HEAD", "clean", worktree_entries(cwd), ...)`; the only differing path, `tracked.py`, is filtered out, and the note omits the deletion.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/stale_why.py:_gate_covered

chunk_findings.detail: `_gate_covered` now filters `paths` through `then is None or p in then`, where `then` is the base commit tree. This drops every path that exists only in the current tree, including newly added tracked files. Example: base has only `a.py`; after `git add b.py`, `differing_paths(then, now)` returns `b.py`, but `b.py not in then`, so `_gate_covered` returns `[]` and the stale note omits the new tracked file. The previous filter `GIT.files(cwd, "tracked")` kept such additions; it needed to be extended to also keep base-tracked deletions, not replaced with base-only membership. As written, a purely additive change in the gate's scope will not mark the gate stale, hiding unreviewed new code.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/stale_why.py:_gate_covered

chunk_findings.detail: The index filter was replaced with `p in then`, and `then` is the reviewed base tree (`commit_tree_entries(cwd, base)`). `differing_paths` still yields additions, so a tracked file the gate would review that did not exist in the base is dropped before the exclude filter. Given a reviewed tree that has only `a.py`, then `git add b.py` (not excluded, not a merge temp): `differing_paths` returns `b.py`, `_gate_covered` returns `[]`, and the stale note stays empty even though the covered code changed. Staged deletions of base files are kept; newly added covered files are not.

chunk_findings.detail: A mode-only change to a `.py` file is classified as trivial even though it is not a docs, format-only, or comment-only edit and can change runtime behavior. Given a commit that only does `chmod +x script.py` (100644 → 100755) on a file whose bytes already contain a shebang, `git diff HEAD -- script.py` is empty, then `_ast_unchanged` compares `git show base:script.py` with `git show HEAD:script.py`; those blobs are identical, so `diff_is_trivial` returns True. The behavior-changing executable-bit change then skips `rubber_duck`, `critic`, and `ci`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:_is_format_or_comment

chunk_findings.detail: The comment-only tier is limited to `*.py` files because `_ast_unchanged` hard-fails at `if not p.endswith(".py"): return False`. A task whose only diff is a comment fix in a non-docs, non-Python file such as `pyproject.toml` still gets `False` from `diff_is_trivial` and pays full cross-family review plus whole-suite `ci`, so the stated new comment-only change tier is not implemented for non-Python comments.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:_ast_unchanged

chunk_findings.detail: The logic-change regression only asserts that at least one of `rubber_duck`, `critic`, or `ci` remains in the pipeline (`or`). A behavior-preserving-tier bug that still leaves `rubber_duck`/`critic` but drops the whole-suite `ci` would satisfy `s.pipeline = ["rubber_duck", "unit_tests"]`, so the test passes even though the stated invariant is that logic changes must still pay full cross-family review **and** whole-suite `ci`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_trivial_tier.py:87 in `test_a_logic_change_does_not_accept_the_trivial_tier`

chunk_findings.detail: `_mode` passes `path` to `git ls-tree` as a pathspec pattern, not as a literal filename. Git treats `ls-tree` path arguments as glob patterns, so for a tracked `.py` file whose name contains a glob metacharacter (e.g. `src/a*.py`), one path can match multiple entries. `_mode` returns only the first entry’s mode. In a repo where `src/a!.py` sorts before `src/a*.py` and both have mode `100644` in base and HEAD, do `chmod +x` only on `src/a*.py` and leave its bytes unchanged. `CO.changed_paths` reports `src/a*.py`; `_mode(base, p)` and `_mode(HEAD, p)` both return `100644` from the first matching entry `src/a!.py`, while `_show` compares the unchanged bytes of `src/a*.py`, so `_ast_unchanged` returns True. This is exactly the behavior-changing executable-bit change the fix is meant to prevent, still misclassified as trivial.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:_mode

chunk_findings.detail: `:(literal){path}` is parsed as long-form pathspec magic, and git consumes one optional colon immediately after `)`. For a tracked file whose name starts with `:`, that colon is the filename, so the lookup silently drops it and reads a different path. Given both `weird.py` and `:weird.py` at mode `100644` in base and HEAD, `chmod +x` only `:weird.py`: `_mode` runs `git ls-tree <ref> -- ':(literal):weird.py'`, which matches `weird.py` (`100644`) on both sides. The mode change is invisible and the change can still be classified trivial, the same wrong-file failure the glob fix was meant to close. A leading-colon name used to fail closed (`:weird.py` is invalid short magic); the new spelling can return another file's mode. `:(literal)./{path}` keeps the colon in the name.

chunk_findings.detail: The guard only treats a dirty tracked file as disqualifying when `p not in paths`, but a dirty tracked file whose path is already in `paths` is equally uncommitted work and is not validated. Example: the committed task diff is a comment-only edit to `foo.py`, so `paths == ["foo.py"]`; then the index contains a staged logic edit to the same `foo.py`. `git diff HEAD --name-only` and `git diff HEAD --cached --name-only` both print `foo.py`, and because `"foo.py" in paths` the `p not in paths` predicate is false, so `_uncommitted_not_in` returns False. `diff_is_trivial` then calls `_is_format_or_comment` on the committed `base..HEAD` range only, sees the comment-only commit, and returns True. chunk_findings.detail: A mode-only change to a `.py` file is classified as trivial even though it is not a docs, format-only, or comment-only edit and can change runtime behavior. Given a commit that only does `chmod +x script.py` (100644 → 100755) on a file whose bytes already contain a shebang, `git diff HEAD -- script.py` is empty, then `_ast_unchanged` compares `git show base:script.py` with `git show HEAD:script.py`; those blobs are identical, so `diff_is_trivial` returns True. The behavior-changing executable-bit change then skips `rubber_duck`, `critic`, and `ci`.

chunk_findings.detail: The comment-only tier is limited to `*.py` files because `_ast_unchanged` hard-fails at `if not p.endswith(".py"): return False`. A task whose only diff is a comment fix in a non-docs, non-Python file such as `pyproject.toml` still gets `False` from `diff_is_trivial` and pays full cross-family review plus whole-suite `ci`, so the stated new comment-only change tier is not implemented for non-Python comments.

chunk_findings.detail: The logic-change regression only asserts that at least one of `rubber_duck`, `critic`, or `ci` remains in the pipeline (`or`). A behavior-preserving-tier bug that still leaves `rubber_duck`/`critic` but drops the whole-suite `ci` would satisfy `s.pipeline = ["rubber_duck", "unit_tests"]`, so the test passes even though the stated invariant is that logic changes must still pay full cross-family review **and** whole-suite `ci`.

chunk_findings.detail: `_mode` passes `path` to `git ls-tree` as a pathspec pattern, not as a literal filename. Git treats `ls-tree` path arguments as glob patterns, so for a tracked `.py` file whose name contains a glob metacharacter (e.g. `src/a*.py`), one path can match multiple entries. `_mode` returns only the first entry’s mode. In a repo where `src/a!.py` sorts before `src/a*.py` and both have mode `100644` in base and HEAD, do `chmod +x` only on `src/a*.py` and leave its bytes unchanged. `CO.changed_paths` reports `src/a*.py`; `_mode(base, p)` and `_mode(HEAD, p)` both return `100644` from the first matching entry `src/a!.py`, while `_show` compares the unchanged bytes of `src/a*.py`, so `_ast_unchanged` returns True. This is exactly the behavior-changing executable-bit change the fix is meant to prevent, still misclassified as trivial.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:_mode

chunk_findings.detail: `:(literal){path}` is parsed as long-form pathspec magic, and git consumes one optional colon immediately after `)`. For a tracked file whose name starts with `:`, that colon is the filename, so the lookup silently drops it and reads a different path. Given both `weird.py` and `:weird.py` at mode `100644` in base and HEAD, `chmod +x` only `:weird.py`: `_mode` runs `git ls-tree <ref> -- ':(literal):weird.py'`, which matches `weird.py` (`100644`) on both sides. The mode change is invisible and the change can still be classified trivial, the same wrong-file failure the glob fix was meant to close. A leading-colon name used to fail closed (`:weird.py` is invalid short magic); the new spelling can return another file's mode. `:(literal)./{path}` keeps the colon in the name.
